title: 5 Dinners Under $3 a Serving (Week 12)
creator: Priya Kaur
description:
Five cheap dinners for a family of four, all under three dollars a serving. Full grocery list and recipes on my blog.

Recipes: https://priyacooksonabudget.com/week12

Shot on a very old phone in a very small kitchen.

sentences.t: Hi friends, welcome back to week twelve of cheap dinners, and we are going fast today because I have five of them.
Dinner number one is a chickpea and spinach curry, and this one costs about a dollar sixty a serving.
Two cans of chickpeas, an onion, garlic, a thumb of ginger, a can of crushed tomatoes, and whatever spinach is about to die in your fridge.
I bloom the spices in the oil first, cumin seeds until they crackle, then turmeric and garam masala for like thirty seconds.
Don't walk away during this part, the spices go from perfect to burnt really quick.
Tomatoes in, chickpeas in, simmer fifteen minutes, spinach at the very end.
My kids ate it, which, if you've watched this channel, you know is the highest award I can give.
Dinner two is sheet pan sausage and potatoes.
I buy the big family pack of sausages when it's on sale and freeze them in fours.
Potatoes cut small so they cook at the same speed as the sausage, plus whatever peppers or onions you have, salt, pepper, smoked paprika.
Four twenty-five for about thirty-five minutes, flip halfway, done.
This one comes out to about two forty a serving, mostly because sausage is not cheap anymore.
Dinner three is my mom's egg fried rice, and the secret is day-old rice, please don't use fresh rice, it goes mushy.
Hot pan, eggs first, scramble them soft and pull them out, then the rice, then frozen peas and carrots, soy sauce, a little sesame oil.
Eggs back in at the end, scallions on top, and that's like ninety cents a serving.
Okay, quick pause before dinner number four, because today's sponsor is Factor.
Look, I love cooking, you know I love cooking, but there are nights where I just cannot.
Factor sends you fully prepared meals, chef-made, dietitian approved, and they're ready in about two minutes.
No chopping, no dishes, no standing in front of the fridge at nine p.m. eating shredded cheese out of the bag.
Head to factormeals.com/priya50 and use code PRIYA50 for fifty percent off your first box.
Okay, dinner four, black bean quesadillas.
This is the one I make when I have literally nothing planned.
Mash a can of black beans with cumin, chili powder, and a squeeze of lime, spread it on a tortilla, cheese on top, fold it over.
Medium heat, a little butter, flip when it's golden.
Serve it with salsa and a big pile of shredded cabbage, because cabbage is the cheapest vegetable in the store and nobody talks about it.
About a dollar thirty a serving.
And dinner five is a big pot of lentil soup, which also covers lunch for the next two days.
Carrots, celery, onion, a bag of brown lentils, a can of tomatoes, and a parmesan rind if you've been saving them, which you should be.
Let it go for forty minutes, and right at the end, a splash of vinegar to wake it up.
That one comes out to about seventy cents a serving, so it pulls the whole week's average way down.
So the total for all five dinners for four people was fifty-one dollars and change.
The grocery list and all the recipes are on the blog, link below.
Tell me in the comments what you want me to try next week, and I'll see you then.
